hints.title: Parabolic Shape Concavity Distinction
hints.text: A quadratic function is a parabola. If coefficient a is non-negative, the maximum values occur at the outer endpoints; if negative, minimum values occur at the outer endpoints.

hints.title: Two Pointers Extreme Inward Convergence
hints.text: Place pointers at the start and end of nums. Compare function values at both pointers and populate the result array from back to front if a is non-negative, or front to back if a is negative.

hints.title: Directional Result Array Filling
hints.text: Compute f(nums[left]) and f(nums[right]). When a is non-negative, assign the larger to result[idx--]; when a is negative, assign the smaller to result[idx++]. Repeat until pointers cross.

hints.title: See the blueprint

complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(N) time and O(1) auxiliary space beyond the output array.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Transforming all values and sorting them takes O(N log N) time, ignoring the sorted input guarantee.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Exploiting the monotonic halves of a parabola enables inward two-pointer placement in O(N) linear time.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize parabola concavity determined by the sign of coefficient a.
